notes.cutoff: Data cut-off: the latest EGX close is Thursday 29 October (EGX30 49,596.14). This evening update adds the CBE's 100 bp hike, Thursday's index and stock closes, and Wednesday's equity and debt flows. Brent is the Thursday morning level quoted by EnterpriseAM. Bullish and bearish tags are directional reads of the news, not trade recommendations.
notes.unverified: Not verified and therefore left out or marked unverified: Thursday's turnover, breadth and investor flows (Amwal Al Ghad's flow figures are in billions and look wrong), Thursday's CBE exchange rate, Thursday's debt flows, the 364-day T-bill yield, the budget's oil assumption, net international reserves and their FX and gold split, the FRA's temporary broker capital floor status, and Egypt's October inflation date.
notes.sourcesFoot: Not used: Amwal Al Ghad's 27 October flow figures (the units look wrong), the Raisin Fed page's jobs figures (they conflict with the Fed statement's wording), and an Asharq Al-Awsat piece on Sudan that is dated December 2025. Pages that failed to open: both CNBC pages, the Washington Times, Zeebiz and Ahram Online. The Herald and Oilprice pages are dated 24 and 23 October and are used only as dated oil context. Mansa Markets' EGX page was not used because its prices are stale (they match the 25 October close).

items: EGP passes 56 per dollar at the CBE (sell 56.3511 on Monday) as foreign and Arab investors net sell about $664 mn of bills and bonds → secondary-market debt selling and regional risk drive the slide; importers lose, USD earners gain, and Thursday's CBE meeting is the test.

EGX30 closes Monday at 48,416.94, down 8.4% in three sessions, and the FRA halves brokers' minimum liquid capital ratio to 5% → foreign selling and forced selling by leveraged holders prompt the regulator to ease the rule through Thursday.

Brent trades near $116 on Tuesday morning, about 55% above the $75 in Egypt's budget (derived) → Hormuz flows run at about 60% of normal and Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia add supply fear, widening Egypt's fuel bill.

Egypt's parliament backs military support for Saudi Arabia while the Houthis keep firing at Riyadh and the Eastern Province → a closer link to the regional war lifts Egypt's risk premium and puts Suez and tourism sentiment at risk.

The Fed decides today with a hold priced at about 93% after September's hike to 3.75–4.00% → a firm Fed keeps foreign holders of Egyptian bills under pressure and leaves the CBE no room to cut on Thursday.
EGP breaks 56 per dollar at the CBE for the first time → foreign sellers of T-bills (net $700.5 mn on Monday) are the driver; importers and leveraged names suffer, USD earners gain.
EGX30 falls 1.66% to 48,416.94, down 8.4% in three sessions; EGX70 fell 11.07% on Sunday → liquidity, margin calls and foreign selling hit small caps hardest; Thursday's CBE meeting is the next test.

Parliament authorises Sisi to give military support to Saudi Arabia after Houthi strikes on Riyadh airport and Aramco sites → raises the regional risk premium on Egyptian assets and keeps Red Sea shipping risk alive for Suez revenue.
Brent sits at $115.41 while the US-Iran war keeps Hormuz under attack → Egypt's energy import bill and fuel subsidy gap widen just as the IMF's final review opens.

Banque du Caire prices its IPO at EGP 5.30 with the largest private tranche in EGX history → strong institutional demand helps the IMF divestment target but absorbs local liquidity before trading starts on 2 November.

key.l: FOMC vote to hold; two dissents for a hike

stories.h: Fed holds at 3.75–4.00% as two members vote for a hike
stories.src: Federal Reserve; Reuters via Yahoo Finance; EnterpriseAM
stories.what: The FOMC keeps the federal funds range at 3.75–4.00% by 10-2. Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack vote for a quarter-point hike. The statement says inflation remains elevated and the Committee will gather more information, and it closes with "The Committee will deliver price stability." Chair Kevin Warsh says eight meetings a year is right, with one 2027 meeting holding no rate vote. After the decision the 2-year yield falls 3.8 bp to 4.7%, the 10-year rises 5 bp to 5.042%, the 30-year rises 6 bp to 5.367% and the dollar index slips 0.2%.
stories.why: Inflation stays above the 2% target after September's hike, and the statement attributes some uncertainty to geopolitical developments. EnterpriseAM says markets largely price a quarter-point hike in December.
stories.aff: The dollar, US yields, emerging-market carry, gold ($4,052, down 0.6% in early Thursday trading) and the CBE's room to move.
stories.eg: A firm Fed narrows the yield gap that holds foreign money in Egyptian bills, which have seen about $1.28 bn of net foreign and Arab selling over Monday and Tuesday.
stories.egx: Bearish for foreign-held blue chips, banks' valuations and rate-sensitive developers.
stories.names: Foreign-held EGX30 blue chips; real estate developers.

stories.h: EGX30 ends the week 0.64% higher as small caps lead and the CBE hikes
stories.src: Amwal Al Ghad; Middle East Observer; StockAnalysis.com
stories.what: The EGX30 closes Thursday at 49,596.14, up 0.64%, after Wednesday's 1.64% fall to 49,281.24. The EGX70 rises 2.77% to 16,779.72 and the EGX100 2.27% to 22,639.93, and market cap reaches EGP 3.892 tn. Among blue chips, AMOC (+4.87%), e-finance (+3.54%) and Sidi Kerir (+2.60%) lead, while Abu Qir Fertilizers (-3.51%), Mopco (-2.50%) and Telecom Egypt (-1.65%) fall. Over five sessions the EGX30 is down about 2.85% (derived).
stories.why: Wednesday's fall comes as foreign institutions net sell EGP 229.1 mn and Egyptian individuals buy EGP 315.6 mn. None of the sources gives a single cause for Thursday's rise, and the CBE decision is announced after the session.
stories.aff: Foreign-held blue chips, small caps and the retail investors who now dominate fund holdings.
stories.eg: Local retail money keeps absorbing foreign selling.
stories.egx: Neutral overall: small caps rebound while fertiliser names and Telecom Egypt lag.
stories.names: AMOC, e-finance, Sidi Kerir (up); Abu Qir, Mopco, Telecom Egypt (down).

key.l: CBE sell rate, EGP per USD, Wed 28 Oct

stories.h: Pound holds past EGP 56 as debt outflows reach $1.28 bn in two days
stories.src: See News; Middle East Observer; EnterpriseAM
stories.what: The CBE average rate is 56.06 buy and 56.20 sell on Wednesday, against 56.21 and 56.35 on Monday, so the pound recovers about 15 piastres on Tuesday. Foreign and Arab investors net sell $619.1 mn of Treasury bills and bonds on Tuesday as of 5 pm (foreign investors sell about $665 mn of bills and $33.6 mn of bonds, offset by $79.5 mn of Arab bill purchases), taking Monday and Tuesday to about $1.28 bn. A banking source says there is no dollar shortage, and the CBE tells banks to put FX towards productive sectors while keeping strategic-goods importers supplied. Net selling slows to $391 mn on Wednesday as of 4 pm, mostly foreign bill sales of $368.45 mn. Egypt's 5-year CDS sits near 357 bps.
stories.why: Continued sovereign-debt selling and regional risk. Thursday's rate and debt flows are not verified.
stories.aff: T-bill yields, import costs, inflation expectations and the CBE's room to move today.
stories.eg: Importers say dollars are available but landed costs and port storage charges keep rising.
stories.egx: Bearish for importers, food and consumer names and foreign-held blue chips; bullish for USD earners.

stories.h: CBE surprises with a 100 bp hike, its first since March 2024
stories.src: See News; Amwal Al Ghad; Zawia3
stories.what: The Monetary Policy Committee raises the overnight deposit rate to 20% and the lending rate to 21%, with the main operation and discount rates at 20.5%. Most analysts expected a sixth straight hold. The next meeting is on 17 December.
stories.why: The committee cites an unfavourable external environment and rising uncertainty, and says it wants to anchor inflation expectations. The move follows the pound's first break past EGP 56 per dollar and about $1.67 bn of foreign and Arab debt selling from Monday to Wednesday (derived from $664 mn, $619.1 mn and $391 mn).
stories.aff: T-bill yields, the carry trade, the pound, bank margins, borrowing costs for developers and leveraged companies, and the appeal of deposits against equities.
stories.eg: A wider real-rate cushion, about 6.1 points over inflation (derived), is meant to win back foreign holders of Egyptian debt.
stories.egx: Bullish for banks' margins over time; bearish for developers, leveraged industrials and consumer-finance lenders. The EGX30 still closes 0.64% higher on Thursday.
stories.names: Banks (CIB, QNB Egypt, HDBK) bullish; developers (TMG, Palm Hills) and NBFIs bearish.

key.l: Banque du Caire retail book coverage

stories.h: Banque du Caire retail book closes 27 times covered ahead of its 2 November debut
stories.what: The retail tranche attracts about 9.29 bn shares of orders against 343.1 mn on offer at EGP 5.30, roughly EGP 49.2 bn of demand for EGP 1.8 bn of stock by EnterpriseAM's conversion. Allocation is pro rata, so applicants receive about 3.7% of their request. The sale is upsized to 45% from 30%. Four foreign funds (Helikon, Redwheel, Sustainable Capital, Waha Investments) commit up to $256 mn as cornerstones, and the IFC and EBRD also buy in. Trading is expected on Monday 2 November, and CI Capital can buy back retail sell orders at EGP 5.30 for 30 days.
stories.why: Local investors want quality state assets at a price analysts call fair: Baker Tilly sets fair value at the offer price, while Arab African International Securities puts it at EGP 7.8 and Ostoul at EGP 6.55 (EnterpriseAM, 27 Oct).
stories.aff: Brokerages, state-bank sentiment, the privatisation programme and local liquidity.
stories.eg: A successful sale supports Egypt's asset-sale targets while foreign selling continues elsewhere.
stories.egx: Bullish for brokerages and sentiment towards state-bank listings; the unallocated cash may also support local buying.
stories.names: Brokerages and investment banks; Banque du Caire.

stories.h: Brent holds near $114 as Gulf attacks and Iran-strike fears keep supply risk alive
stories.what: Brent trades at $114.40, up 0.5%, in early Thursday trading. That is about 2.0% below Friday 24 October's close of $116.72, its highest level since April (derived). Brent is up about 20% since early September.
stories.why: Context from last week: prices rose on a New York Times report that the US and Israel have drawn up plans to resume strikes on Iran after the November midterms, and on Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including an Aramco evacuation at Dhahran (Herald, 24 Oct; Oilprice, 23 Oct). Iran has increased attacks on tankers in Hormuz. Neither page is from the last 24 hours.
stories.aff: Egypt's fuel bill, the subsidy gap, global inflation, shipping costs and the pound.
stories.eg: Fuel prices are frozen through December, so the cost builds up on the state's books.
stories.egx: Bearish for importers and energy-intensive industry such as construction materials; oil-linked names have held up better.

stories.h: Egypt plans 15 mn barrels of crude on supplier credit as refineries run harder
stories.what: Egypt plans to import about 15 mn barrels in 4Q, 8% more than a year earlier, for $1.4–1.5 bn (6 mn barrels in October, 4.5 mn each in November and December), from Saudi Arabia, Libya, Greece and others, paid through short- and medium-term credit. Refinery utilisation rises above 80% from 66%, and the ministry aims to cut product imports to $3.6 bn from $6.2 bn in FY 2025/26. Apache plans five wells for 70 mmcf/d in 1Q 2027, against natural depletion of about 120 mmcf/d a month.
stories.why: Domestic output of about 527k bbl/d and falling gas output leave a gap that imports fill; gas drove most of last year's $4.7 bn rise in the oil import bill.
stories.aff: EGPC's finances, the dollar need, refiners and gas suppliers.
stories.eg: Supplier credit eases the immediate dollar demand but adds to short-term obligations.
stories.egx: Neutral overall; a cost headwind for fuel-intensive industry, a mild positive for refining throughput.

key.l: container capacity using Suez or the Cape that used the canal, early Oct

stories.h: Suez recovery stays slow as Maersk eyes March 2027 for a full return
stories.what: About 36% of container capacity moving through Suez or around the Cape used the canal in early October, against 80% before the Red Sea crisis. Maersk expects all its services back on the canal by March 2027. The edition also notes that Suez disruption adds cost and lead time for Egyptian brands selling abroad.
stories.why: Houthi attacks and the wider regional war keep carriers cautious.
stories.aff: Suez Canal revenue, container lines and exporters' shipping costs.
stories.eg: Lower canal traffic means less dollar income for the state at a time of heavy outflows.
stories.egx: Mildly bearish for the pound and for logistics; no listed company is named in the source.

key.l: seats for Netanyahu's bloc, short of 61

stories.h: Israel's election leaves a deadlock and Arab parties with a record number of seats
stories.what: Netanyahu's bloc holds 54 of 120 seats with counting still under way, short of the 61 needed, and Arab parties have a record 17 seats so far. Israel Hayom says neither bloc can form a government without the Arab parties, that Gadi Eisenkot is the likely candidate to try, and that Avigdor Lieberman must decide whether to drop his veto on a government backed by Arab parties. A military confrontation with Iran could push parties towards a unity government.
stories.why: A fragmented vote and high Arab turnout leave both blocs without a majority.
stories.aff: Israeli coalition talks, regional diplomacy and possibly a new election.
stories.eg: The sources do not discuss Egypt; any effect on Gaza diplomacy is not reported.
stories.egx: Neutral. No direct EGX channel is reported.

stories.h: Retail investors now hold 79.8% of fund certificates as money market growth stalls
stories.what: Fund net asset value rises 7.16% quarter on quarter to EGP 504.71 bn, and assets under management rise 7.27% to EGP 512.84 bn across 232 funds. Money market funds, about 60% of assets, grow only 2.1% to EGP 303.12 bn, which Azimut Egypt's Ahmed Abou El Saad reads as net outflows. Index funds grow 82.6% to EGP 13.14 bn and precious-metals funds grow 26.6% to EGP 11.92 bn. Equity funds return 5.55% on average in 3Q, down from 17.66% in 2Q. Retail investors' share of certificates rises to 79.8% from 74.7%.
stories.why: Retail savers are moving out of cash-like funds into index and gold products as returns on equities cool.
stories.aff: Brokers, asset managers and the EGX's retail-driven turnover.
stories.eg: The EGX is now more dependent on retail sentiment as foreign investors sell.
stories.egx: Mildly bullish for brokers and asset managers; leaves index-heavy names exposed to retail sentiment.

stories.h: Cabinet grants golden licences to 1.8 GW of wind as solar-storage projects advance
stories.what: The Cabinet approves golden licences for two 900 MW wind projects, Shadwan and Shokeir. Nefer Minya closes $566 mn of debt and starts full construction on its 1.2 GWp solar plant, while Dandara signs preliminary financing terms for a $650 mn, 1 GW solar and 200 MWh storage project. From April 2027, consumer finance companies must also check an I-Score before approving financing.
stories.why: Gas demand averages 6.2 bcf/d and peaks near 7.5 bcf/d in summer, while natural depletion is about 120 mmcf/d a month, according to EnterpriseAM's crude import article, which pushes Egypt towards new supply sources.
stories.aff: Renewable developers, contractors, cable and electrical suppliers, and consumer-finance lenders.
stories.eg: More renewables eventually reduce the gas and fuel import need.
stories.egx: Neutral to mildly bullish for contractors and electrical suppliers over time; neutral for consumer finance.
stories.names: Contractors and electrical suppliers (sector); consumer finance (sector).

week.event: Banque du Caire expected to start trading on the EGX
week.why: A test of local liquidity after a 27-times covered retail book; CI Capital stabilises at EGP 5.30 for 30 days.

week.event: Notice period for Alamal Alsharif's EGX main-market listing ends
week.why: The company files to list with EGP 796.3 mn of issued capital; state banks own 54.5%.
Oil traders fear renewed US-Israeli strikes on Iran after the vote; Brent is near $114.

week.event: CBE Monetary Policy Committee, last meeting of 2026
week.why: The first test of whether Thursday's 100 bp hike is a one-off or the start of a cycle.
The freeze runs through December; a rise in fuel prices after that would lift costs across industry.

week.event: Maersk expects all services back on the Suez Canal
week.why: A full return would restore canal revenue; traffic is at 36% of container capacity now.
